# Foldex patch on eframe 0.36.2

Base: the pinned crates.io eframe 0.36.2 source, with its original MIT/Apache licenses retained.

`src/native/wgpu_integration.rs`, `render_immediate_viewport`: apply the ordinary viewport path's visibility and requested-action handling to immediate child windows. Invisible retained windows skip tessellation/GPU submission/presentation. Visible child windows pass screenshot requests to the painter and drain cut/copy/paste actions rather than accumulating them. Platform output and viewport commands still run while hidden, so reopening remains possible.

Texture deltas now share one context-wide pending queue across ordinary and immediate viewports. Texture IDs and the font atlas are global to the context. Keeping updates in separate hidden-window queues could withhold required uploads, then replay older atlas pixels after newer updates. The next visible viewport flushes the shared queue in production order. There is no hidden-window upload or presentation loop.

Immediate input also inherits the active parent's actual `max_texture_side`. Immediate viewports bypass `App::raw_input_hook`; previously Foldex's root used a 2048 atlas while its immediate child reverted to the GPU maximum. Opening the launcher repeatedly recreated the shared font atlas, invalidating retained text and repeating font setup work. Both now use the same bounded atlas.

Visibility includes the last queued Visible command in the current immediate-viewport output. A child created hidden can paint its first frame before Visible(true) is applied; this avoids exposing a blank first frame while preserving the idle hidden-window optimization.

The upstream immediate path unconditionally painted and passed an empty screenshot vector. Foldex's first native launcher workload reached calculation/settings, then timed out awaiting a capture (`b92-launcher-01.metrics.json`). The launcher keeps one native child window for fast reopening; rendering it after closing would add work to ordinary explorer frames. The local patch is confined to this backend path and adds no dependency packages or background work.

Screenshots are delivered through the painter's capture queue into input events, tagged with their originating viewport. The opt-in Foldex benchmark handles those events at the root input hook and writes only its owned launcher images. Ordinary use requests no captures.

`src/native/run.rs`, `WinitAppWrapper::new_events`: install the same event-loop context as the other event handlers before checking timer repaint deadlines. On Windows that check directly renders invisible windows, and a cold immediate child needs the current `ActiveEventLoop` to create its window. Without this context, the immediate renderer returned before calling the UI callback, reaching egui's `user callback was never called` panic. This fixes the missing backend context; it does not catch or suppress the panic.

`App::run_ui_when_hidden` is a default-false, event-driven opt-in used by Foldex while its immediate launcher is open. Both native renderers honor it for the root UI, while still skipping paint for a minimized or occluded root. Foldex's `App::logic` can service a tray activation and request the next UI pass without showing the explorer. Native-hidden children no longer count as visible descendants, so retaining a closed launcher does not force the minimized root UI to run.

The opt-in `foldex --probe-lifecycle <new-output-directory>` workload owns its windows, state and generated folder. It creates no real tray icon, global shortcut, clipboard listener or normal session. It minimizes the root, closes its final tab, verifies logic-only wakes, opens the cold immediate launcher through a simulated tray event, performs four close/reopen cycles on the same HWND, restores the explorer, and saves before explicit Quit. `report.json` records the checks after clean backend exit; a real panic writes the probe-owned `foldex-crash.log`.

Append `--visible-minimized-root` in a separate probe run to keep the explorer logically and natively visible while minimized. This independently exercises a cold immediate launcher and four reopen cycles without closing the last tab or hiding the root first. Both variants must observe logic-only wakes with no root UI callbacks before opening the cold child, and share the same 15-second deadline.

`src/native/run.rs` now consumes an existing repaint deadline before a synchronous Windows resize paint or an OS redraw. Previously the synchronous path inserted an immediate deadline before painting, so every `WM_SIZE` also requested a second redraw afterward. Repaint requests produced by the new pass still arrive through the normal proxy; child-to-parent repaint forwarding and the invisible-window path are preserved.

`App::repaint_on_window_move` is a default-true Windows opt-out for applications whose client content is independent of native screen position. Both native backends refresh viewport information and forward move events to egui-winit/accessibility before honoring the opt-out. A move can reuse the compositor's existing surface without waiting for another GPU presentation. DPI, resize, input and application repaint requests remain active. This also avoids scheduling a redundant redraw from the `Moved` event that winit emits before `Resized` during left/top edge sizing. Applications retain upstream behavior unless they explicitly opt out.

The matching Foldex frame procedure retains a zero `WM_NCCALCSIZE` result for its integrated-caption frame, which has no top non-client inset when restored. A previous `WVR_REDRAW` policy discarded native client preservation during a resize and was reverted after visible right/bottom gaps were reported. Chromium's native frame handler also retains zero when the top or left inset is zero. Maximize/fullscreen transitions and the single-RECT form keep the same result. The procedure acknowledges `WM_ERASEBKGND` without mixing a GDI blank frame into DXGI flip-model presentation, and leaves resize repaint scheduling to winit instead of requesting additional egui passes from both `WM_SIZING` and `WM_SIZE`. Correct transient buffer/target coverage must come from the presentation scaling policy; this handler cannot make two compositor transactions atomic.

Primary references: [WM_NCCALCSIZE return values](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/wm-nccalcsize), [WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGED and WM_SIZE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/wm-windowposchanged), [DXGI flip-model API interop limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3ddxgi/for-best-performance--use-dxgi-flip-model), [Chromium's native frame handler](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/ui/views/win/hwnd_message_handler.cc), and the pinned winit 0.30.13 Windows event-loop source. These changes address event scheduling and native pixel preservation; API timing and application geometry probes do not establish compositor-displayed frame timing.

Windows wgpu frames now retain one physical client-size snapshot through input collection, in both the ordinary and immediate viewport paths. The snapshot supplies `RawInput::screen_rect` at the input's native pixels-per-point and egui zoom, and updates the viewport's inner-rectangle size. The painter's framebuffer extent then follows the completed UI's `input_for(viewport_id).viewport_rect()` times its `FullOutput::pixels_per_point`, rounded to physical pixels. This normally equals the raw snapshot, but also handles egui replacing that screen rect with its previous canvas when a pending zoom and native resize coincide. The raw zero-size/minimize guard remains authoritative. The explicit viewport ID is required because an immediate child's completion restores the active parent context. Queued `Resized` events still trigger synchronous Windows repaint and resize lifecycle handling, but their possibly stale dimensions no longer configure a different framebuffer independently. No later HWND size query controls the extent used to paint already-generated geometry.

Each viewport caches the last extent actually applied to the painter. Identical frame extents skip configuration, avoiding `ResizeBuffers` and present/GPU idle waits on ordinary frames. New windows begin with an invalid cache, including the root whose custom native frame can change its client insets during app creation. Window recreation invalidates every cache because `Painter::set_window(None)` clears all surfaces; suspension invalidates the Windows caches too. The painter's internal lost-surface recovery preserves its existing width and height. The visible paint path ensures a surface exists before applying the completed UI extent. Zero-sized snapshots and hidden retained windows neither configure/present nor advance the cache; texture updates and platform/viewport commands retain their existing queues and lifecycle. Other platforms retain event-driven sizing.

Ordinary Windows GPU painting additionally checks actual native visibility, the last queued `Visible` command, and the integration's existing first-frame state. Ordinary visible startup still paints before `post_rendering` reveals the root; explicitly hidden startup has no first-frame exception. A queued reveal paints before applying the command, while a queued hide suppresses painting and cancels any automatic startup reveal. UI eligibility is unchanged, so a hidden secondary root can queue its initial placement/reveal and a hidden parent can service visible immediate children. Root GPU work remains skipped while those children are hosted.

Focused `frame_size_tests` cover the observed 36-by-20-pixel size mismatch across fractional DPI, shrink/grow snapshots, duplicate-frame configuration suppression, zero-size rejection and invalidation, plus a real egui pending-zoom/resize pass. These exercise the size contract and configuration decisions; root-owned displayed-window captures must still verify footer/content alignment and rule out cleared client strips.

`NativeOptions::windows_no_redirection_bitmap` is a default-false Windows wgpu option. A shared helper preserves egui-winit attribute conversion, monitor selection and post-creation initialization, adding `with_no_redirection_bitmap` before creating the HWND. Root and deferred/immediate/recreated windows use it; shared state retains the option and detached app processes receive the same main policy. Foldex enables it only with its selected DX12 DxgiFromVisual presentation. Generic wgpu/glow defaults remain unchanged. GPU visibility, hidden-root UI hosting, shared texture queues and per-frame extent handling retain their existing behavior.

Foldex's live native resize can now paint before returning from `WM_NCCALCSIZE`, when Win32 still reports the previous client geometry. `with_windows_early_resize` owns a scoped thread-local HWND/client-rectangle hint; the ordinary input path claims it only for that HWND and replaces both physical size and the viewport's client origin. No stack pointer, window property, retained application callback, or winit registry modification is used. A render-depth guard covers the entire ordinary paint entry and immediate child paints, and the API also declines while an eframe event-loop callback is active. Programmatic resize during UI work keeps the ordinary resize fallback.

The native frame invokes this only for changed nonempty dimensions during visible, restored, no-redirection live sizing. Existing insets and the zero `WM_NCCALCSIZE` result remain intact. Its synchronous `WM_PAINT` uses winit's existing idle-handler dispatch and reentrancy deferral. The hint expires on return or unwind. An acknowledgement requires a claimed hint, a completed UI extent matching the configured painter extent and proposal, plus caller verification of a new successful native HWND/extent presentation. Pending zoom, skipped/failed/deferred painting, hidden/minimized windows and destroyed frames retain the normal paint fallback. The next `Resized` event consumes the acknowledgement only if its dimensions and the actual screen-space client rectangle match; platform, geometry and accessibility bookkeeping still run before suppressing that duplicate repaint. Frame removal/destruction clears outstanding state.

Focused `windows_resize::tests` cover owner isolation, one-time hint/ack consumption, nested render and hint rejection, skipped/failed/mismatched completion, geometry mismatch, destruction and unwind cleanup. Displayed-window validation remains separate. This follows the early-presentation principle in the open [winit #4740](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4740) and [wgpu #10548](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/pull/10548) experiments while preserving the custom frame's own client calculation and the confirmed DirectComposition topology.
